advisor_identified: Cynthia E. Milton, historian of Latin America at Université de Montréal, later University of Victoria.

doctorate.title: The many meanings of poverty: Colonial compacts and social assistance in eighteenth-century Quito

evidence.says: The History faculty profile identifies Cynthia E. Milton as a former Montréal history professor and lists her Wisconsin–Madison history credential in 2002.
The university biography explicitly states that Milton holds a PhD in History from Wisconsin–Madison.
The departmental bibliography attributes the thesis title recorded above to Cynthia E. Milton and gives PhD, University of Wisconsin–Madison, 2002; its catalogue source is ProQuest.
The indexed thesis front matter for Hélène Rompré’s 2011 Montréal dissertation, matching the first student title in the entry, names Cynthia Milton as research supervisor.

notes: Institution, year, author and main title match the linked AHA record. The Montréal bibliography gives the subtitle as “Colonial compacts and social assistance in eighteenth-century Quito,” whereas AHA gives “Colonial Compacts and Social Assistance in Urban Quito.” Bibliography and student front-matter evidence were available through indexed source text; direct retrieval failed.
